findings.reason: Both authentic original standalone tiles contain the complete interval-lift and deck-translation argument but no diagram. Three disjoint open translates mapping to the same quotient arc materially clarify how an evenly covered neighborhood differs from a single global sheet, and the translation arrow makes the quotient invariance explicit. This is a warranted explanatory diagram under the expanded editorial criterion, not a claim that the existing proof was incomplete.
findings.action: Appended a final Remarks section with a schematic real-line-to-quotient-circle TikZ illustration, three open sheets, restricted quotient maps and the integer-translation relation.

correction: Added only the final explanatory Remarks section; preserved all original title, statement, facts, verification proof and frontmatter bytes.

diagram_math_checks.objects: q:R→R/Z; an open interval I of length below 1; U=q[I]; the sheets I−1, I and I+1.
diagram_math_checks.check: Step 1.1 defines q by integer-difference equivalence. Step 2.1 proves disjointness of I+k for all integer k and q^{-1}(U)=union_k(I+k); the three depicted intervals are a finite selection, with ellipses indicating the remaining sheets. The caption explicitly retains openness and the length bound.

diagram_math_checks.maps: q restricted to I−1, I and I+1, each with codomain U.
diagram_math_checks.check: Each restriction lands in U because q(x+k)=q(x). Injectivity follows since distinct points in I differ by less than 1 and cannot differ by a nonzero integer. Each restriction is onto U by translating a representative in I. The local evenly-covered conclusion of step 2.1 and the orbit-map theorem proof step 2.1 supply the homeomorphism interface; def-covering-map-and-evenly-covered-neighbourhoods defines precisely these sheets and restricted homeomorphisms. The downward arrows have these domains/codomains, not maps between different sheets.

diagram_math_checks.map: tau_1:R→R, x↦x+1, carrying I to I+1; tau_n:R→R for n∈Z.
diagram_math_checks.check: The top arrow is directed from I toward I+1. Step 3.1 gives each translation as a homeomorphism and q∘tau_n=q; equivalence by integer difference from step 1.1 verifies the displayed relation directly. The diagram does not suggest fractional shifts are deck transformations.

diagram_math_checks.geometric_data: Open endpoint rings for the three lifted intervals and the quotient arc; schematic circle for R/Z.
diagram_math_checks.check: Because I is open and has length below 1, its endpoints are distinct modulo Z and excluded from q[I]. All eight endpoint rings remain unfilled in the compiled SVG. The circle is explicitly identified as schematic in the caption; no additional circle-identification theorem, orientation convention or global inverse is used in the original proof.

diagram_math_checks.proof_independence: The original four numbered Verification steps remain byte-identical; the illustration is outside Facts and Verification in final Remarks and asserts only the existing local-sheet and integer-translation relations.
